newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Hoechst profit rise, spin off tipped.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Hoechst profit rise, spin off tipped.

text.p: Hoechst AG, Europe's largest chemicals group, is likely to post a 28 percent jump in 1996 operating profits to 4.6 billion marks ($3.1 billion), business magazine Capital reported on Tuesday.
Quoting internal planning documents from Hoechst, Capital said the chemical group's sales in 1996 would be 51 billion marks, slightly lower than in 1995.
The magazine also said Hoechst was planning to spin off its specialty chemicals business into a separate unit although the timing had not been decided.
Hoechst has already said that it plans to spin off its health unit HMR into a separate legal entity and would at some point list it on the bourse.

A Hoechst spokesman said that the profits prediction had been hinted at earlier by chief financial officer Klaus Schmider. He added that the group had already discussed separating off units, including the specialty chemicals division, at this year's general meeting.
Capital said the big contributor to operating profits in 1996 would be Hoechst's health division, where operating profits would increase to 1.7 billion marks, three times higher than in 1995.
It said Hoechst's colorants, pigments and other chemical sectors had been core businesses until the beginning of the 1990s.

Since then a move to Southeast Asia and Central and Eastern Europe by major customers, especially in the textile and clothing industries, had led to speciality chemical products being made increasingly by local producers.
This had led to Hoechst having to close many of its specialty chemical businesses since then, as they were no longer competitive, it added.
